\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{നിർത്തുക} (nirttuka)}{നിർത്തുക (nirttuka)}]{\ml{നിർത്തുക} (nirttuka) — to stop}

\label{lesson:ML-C174-nirttuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to teach, then the Malayalam for to begin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{നിർത്തുക}}
\textbf{\ml{നിർത്തുക}} — \emph{nirttuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to stop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{നിർത്തുക}} (\emph{nirttuka}) is native Dravidian, the causative of the verb \textquotedblleft{}to stand\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}make stand\textquotedblright{}; DEDR 3675 lists the root with Tamil \emph{nil} and Kannada \emph{nil}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nirttuka}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to teach, then the Malayalam for to begin, then say \emph{nirttuka} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കാത്തിരിക്കുക} (kāttirikkuka)}{കാത്തിരിക്കുക (kāttirikkuka)}]{\ml{കാത്തിരിക്കുക} (kāttirikkuka) — to wait}

\label{lesson:ML-C174-kattirikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to begin, then the Malayalam for to stop.

Say \textquotedblleft{}a story.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{Katha}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കാത്തിരിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കാത്തിരിക്കുക}} — \emph{kāttirikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to wait\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കാത്തിരിക്കുക}} (\emph{kāttirikkuka}) is native Dravidian, \textquotedblleft{}sit watching\textquotedblright{}: the verb \textquotedblleft{}to guard, watch, wait\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1416, with Tamil \emph{kā}) joined to the verb \textquotedblleft{}to sit, to be\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 480, with Tamil \emph{iru}).
\end{cousinweb}
